1. Nat Rev Neurosci. 2002 Aug;3(8):655-66. doi: 10.1038/nrn894.

How do you feel? Interoception: the sense of the physiological condition of the 
body.

Craig AD.

As humans, we perceive feelings from our bodies that relate our state of 
well-being, our energy and stress levels, our mood and disposition. How do we 
have these feelings? What neural processes do they represent? Recent functional 
anatomical work has detailed an afferent neural system in primates and in humans 
that represents all aspects of the physiological condition of the physical body. 
This system constitutes a representation of 'the material me', and might provide 
a foundation for subjective feelings, emotion and self-awareness.
